dedupe_keys.name: housing unit and urbanization estimates for the continental u s in consistent tract boundaries 1940 2019

description: Housing unit and urbanization estimates for the continental U.S. in consistent tract boundaries, 1940–2019 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Scott N. Markley et al. Subcounty housing unit counts are important for studying geo-historical patterns of (sub)urbanization, land-use change, and residential loss and gain. The most commonly used subcounty geographical unit for social research in the United States is the census tract. However, the changing geometries and historically incomplete coverage of tracts present significant obstacles for longitudinal analysis that existing datasets do not sufficiently address. Coverage: national (US); published in 2022. Formats: CSV, Shapefile, GeoJSON. The data are held in OSF and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
